step2_answer: ANSWER: The answer depends on the type of plan, so I have not given a single band. (1) BDA's development schemes: the law requires BDA to send each scheme notification to 'the Corporation'. The Corporation has 30 days to make representations. Representations go to the Government through BDA, and BDA must consider them before submitting the scheme for sanction. If no representation arrives in time, the Corporation's concurrence is deemed given. This is mandatory consultation with a duty to consider, not a real right of approval: the Corporation's silence counts as consent, and a representation does not stop the scheme going forward. (2) Works for further development: the Corporation 'shall be consulted' if the area lies within the City limits. This is mandatory consultation with no duty to respond. (3) Private layouts within Corporation limits: BDA needs the Corporation's concurrence. If they disagree, the Government decides. This is a sanction of private layouts, not a plan BDA prepares itself. (4) Master plan under the T&CP Act: the sections I read give the local authority no role in preparing the master plan, only public notice and public comments. On top of this, the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act makes GBA itself the Planning Authority for the Greater Bengaluru Area 'notwithstanding anything contained in any other law'. GBA can also issue binding directions to BDA. These are ULG powers over BDA, but they are not a duty on BDA to prepare its plans jointly with GBA. | EVI

step2_answer: ANSWER: BMTC has no environmental duty in its own law. The 1950 Road Transport Corporations Act, under which BMTC was set up, gives it a general duty to run an efficient, adequate, economical and properly co-ordinated service, with no environmental element. That Act counts BMTC as an 'Urban Transport Agency' (public agencies providing urban mobility, which includes bus systems). It ties BMTC's investment planning to a Comprehensive Mobility Plan built around 'sustainable urban transport' and 'clean' transport. step2_answer: ANSWER: None of the sources we have gives the city government (GBA or its City Corporations) a seat on BMTC's Board. (1) The enabling Act leaves every appointment to the State Government and only requires seats for the Central and State Governments. step2_answer: ANSWER: GMRC's official records show one substantive Managing Director, Shri S. S. Rathore, from at least 1 April 2022 to October 2026. That covers about 4.5 of the last five years. The records do not cover roughly October 2021 to March 2022, and they do not give the date he was appointed. If he was also MD for that gap, the count is 1 (score 10). If someone else was, the count is 2 or more (score 5, or 0 if more than 3). The count, and so the score, cannot be settled from these sources. No acting or additional-charge MD appears anywhere in them. The Joint MD, Sanjay Gupta (from 21-12-2024), works under the MD and is not the chief executive. | EVIDENCE: (1) Who the chief executive is, by function. GMRC-25, FY2022-23 Annual Report, Board's Report XII, p.45: the MD is the Government of Gujarat's nominee, approved in advance by the Government of India and appointed by the Board; 'The general powers of Management are vested in the Managing Director'. The Chairman is the Secretary of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, ex officio and part-time, so he is not the executive head. GMRC-03, the RTI disclosure under s.4(1)(b): 'The day-to-day management of the company in entrusted to the Managing Director'. (2) FY2022-23 (GMRC-25, XIII, pp.45-47): the list of director changes for 1 Apr 2022 to 31 Mar 2023 includes no change of MD, and the key managerial personnel list shows 'MANAGING DIRECTOR - Shri S. S. Rathore'. The FY2023-24 changes up to the AGM show no MD change either. (3)

comments:
SCORE LEFT BLANK. I can't settle how many Managing Directors GMRC had across the whole five-year window from the Citation Sheet alone.

What the sources support (I checked the Step 2 answer against them and it holds):
(1) The MD is the chief executive. GMRC-25 p.45 says: 'The general powers of Management are vested in the Managing Director'. The Chairman is the MoHUA Secretary, ex officio, so he is not the chief executive.
(2) S. S. Rathore was the only MD across FY2022-23:
- GMRC-25 pp.45-47: no MD appears among the director changes for 1-Apr-2022 to 31-Mar-2023, and he is the MD in the s.203 KMP list.
- GMRC-25 p.75, MGT-9 VI.A: the remuneration table puts no 'w.e.f.' or 'upto' date against Rathore. Other directors have those dates, which suggests he held the post for the full year.
- GMRC-25: the changes for FY2023-24 up to the AGM include no MD change.
(3) GMRC-06 (FY2023-24) and GMRC-05 (FY2024-25) both show Rathore as MD. GMRC-05 records a Joint MD, Sanjay Gupta, from 21-12-2024. He is a functional director who signs alongside the MD, so I did not count him.
(4) GMRC-04, the website page last updated 12-Oct-2026, still lists 'Shri S. S. Rathore Managing Director'.

What is missing: no source gives the date Rathore was appointed, and none covers about Oct 2021 to Mar 2022. I checked:
- GMRC-25: Board's Report, KMP list, MGT-9 remuneration table and AOC-2; Note-25 (related party disclosures) is only referred to and its text is not in the extract.
- GMRC-03: the RTI s.4(1)(b) disclosure, which names no MD and gives no dates.
- GMRC-04: the board page.
- Searches across all sources for appointment, tenure and additional-charge wording.
There is no FY2021-22 annual report and no MD appointment order. The score would be 10 if Rathore was MD for the whole window and 5 if there were 2-3 MDs. I can't tell which, so I left it blank rather than guess.

For a person to check:
(a) Get Rathore's appointment date, and any acting or additional-charge MD between Oct 2021 and Mar 2022, from the FY2021-22 Annual Report or an RTI to the GMRC PIO.
(b) Confirm the end date of the five-year window.
(c) Confirm that the Joint MD is not treated as a chief executive.
(d) Confirm that GMRC is in scope for Surat while Surat Phase-1 is still being built.

Minor point: in the GMRC-25 remuneration table Prashant Rao is marked 'Upto 21.02.2022', but the Board's Report gives 21-Feb-2023. This looks like a typo and doesn't affect the MD count.

step2_answer: ANSWER: The most recent official staffing record we have puts BMRDA's sanctioned strength at 56 posts on 31.03.2023. Of these, 27 were filled and 29 were vacant. That is a fill rate of 27 / 56 x 100 = 48.21%, which falls in the 40%–59% band (Score 2). This is a three-year-old snapshot (FY 2022-23). The question asks about current staffing (rules version September 2026), and no later figure is in the Citation Sheet. So no score is proposed. | EVIDENCE: BMRDA-03, Annual Report of BMRDA for 2022-23 (01-04-2022 to 31-03-2023), a Legislature Paper, para 11 'Staff position', page 15: 'The sanctioned staff strength for the Authority as on the 31.03.2023 is 56, out of this, only 27 posts have been filled up and the remaining 29 posts are vacant.' The same paragraph says post-by-post details are in Annexure-1 (page 16). Calculation: filled 27 / sanctioned 56 = 0.4821, so 48.21%. Other sources checked with no staffing figures: the BMRDA website pages BMRDA-05 (Home), BMRDA-06 (Contact Us), BMRDA-07 (Local Planning Areas) and BMRDA-12 (official site).
